{{Quote|I am Rakata&mdash;it is the name of my people. Eons ago, our Infinite Empire ruled this world and so many others.|[[The Imprisoned One]]|<ref name="TOR:TTCF">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|The Thing Czerka Found|Tatooine}}</ref>}}
The '''Infinite Empire''', also known as the '''Rakatan Empire''', or the '''Rakata Empire''', was a [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] spanning [[Politics/Legends|empire]] in [[Galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] ruled by the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]], an advanced [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] that used their knowledge to conquer and [[Slavery/Legends|enslave]] other species throughout the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], until its collapse in [[25,200 BBY]] after a [[Rakatan Civil War|civil war]], paving the way for the formation of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] within several short centuries.

==History==
===Origins===
{{Quote|The Rakata are a pestilence upon the galaxy that, to our shame, we, the Kwa, unleashed.|[[A'nang]]|<ref name="DOTJ PB 4" />}}
Many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before [[36,453 BBY]], the [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]]&mdash;a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]&mdash;arrived on [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]], the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] species, via their [[Infinity Gate]] technology that allowed the Kwa to travel instantaneously across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. As they had done on many worlds before, the Kwa became the Rakata's benefactors, teaching them about [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and giving them advanced technology. However, the Kwa were horrified to realize that Rakata were a cannibalistic race that ignored the Kwa teachings of balance, drawing only on the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Pairing their aggression and desire for conquest with the Kwa technology, the Rakata expanded out from Lehon and began to conquer other worlds in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].<ref name="DOTJ PB 4" />

[[File:Battle_of_Lehon.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Kwa battle the Rakata.]]
The Infinite Empire, as the Rakata called themselves, targeted worlds that were rich with the Force, which they conquered and then enslaved the populations of. The Rakata developed technology that allowed them to induce fear and hatred in Force-sensitive beings, and they used the Force-sensitive [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] among the populations they conquered to fuel their warships and technology by placing them in machines that converted the slaves' dark side emotions into energy. Desiring the Kwa's Infinity Gate technology, they turned on their benefactors when the Kwa refused&mdash;and in the [[Battle between the Kwa and the Rakata|resultant battle]] on Lehon, many Kwa [[Death/Legends|died]] holding off the Rakatan warriors so that they could destroy the gate on Lehon.<ref name="DOTJ PB 4" />

However, the Rakata were not to be stopped. Building an enormous [[Space station/Legends|space station]] known as the [[Star Forge]] over the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Abo]] in the [[Lehon system]]&mdash;a factory powered by the dark side that produced warships and technology for the Empire&mdash;the Rakata spread out over the Unknown Regions and into the eastern [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] by [[35,000 BBY]]. The forest world of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] was one world captured by the Empire, and the Rakata installed a [[Builder Forge|terraforming computer]] on the planet to manipulate Kashyyyk's [[Wroshyr tree/Legends|wroshyr trees]]. However, the computer lost contact with the Rakata in [[33,598 BBY]], and [[33,357 BBY|over two hundred years later]] it malfunctioned, causing a hyper-acceleration in the growth of the wroshyrs.<ref name="KOTOR" />

===Era of conquest===
{{Quote|Long ago the Rakata ruled all the known galaxy; all species bowed down to us.|Keeper [[Orsaa]]|<ref name="KOTOR" />}}
[[File:Infinite_Empire_fleet.png|thumb|right|200px|The fleet of the Infinite Empire]]
By [[30,000 BBY]],<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the Infinite Empire had reached its zenith, linking over five hundred<ref name="History 5">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 05: Rise of the Infinite Empire}}</ref> Force-rich worlds all across the galaxy. During the [[Annexation of Kwa holdings|annexation]] of the [[Kwa holdings]], the Rakata brutally subjugated Dathomir, the homeworld of the Kwa,<ref name="Atlas" /> in revenge for the Kwa's destruction of their Infinity Gates across the galaxy,<ref name="DOTJ PB 4" /> and as a result the Kwa eventually devolved into the simpleminded [[Kwi]] lizards.<ref name="NEC" /> According to the beliefs of the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]], the usage of the Kwa Infinity Gates created unnatural voids and wounds to Dathomir that saw the [[Spirit (Nightsisters)|Spirits]] call the Infinite Empire to the planet. Their arrival decimated the Kwa who were transformed into an animal state by the action of the Spirits.<ref name="BoS:SftDS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> Intrigued by the enormous [[Rancor/Legends|rancors]] native to Dathomir, the Infinite Empire transported a number of them back to Lehon as curiosities, and they also succeeded in [[Defeat of the Gree Empire|driving]] the [[Gree (species)/Legends|Gree]]&mdash;another spacefaring species at the [[Time/Legends|time]]&mdash;all the way back to their [[Gree Enclave/Legends|home cluster]].<ref name="Atlas" /> The Infinite Empire introduced a rancor to the planet [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]], where it became a mythological creature in the culture of the native [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]].<ref name="Barely">{{SW|url=news/barely-tolerable-alien-henchmen-of-the-empire-part-2|series=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>

The Infinite Empire turned the planet [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] into a prison world, using stasis technology to entomb monsters, warlords, and other powerful entities.<ref name="History of Belsavis Prison">{{TORcite|type=codex|History of Belsavis Prison}}</ref> The first prisoner of Belsavis&mdash;and the reason the prison was constructed&mdash;was the [[World Razer]], a mysterious being whose hunger supposedly consumed a thousand worlds. According to inscriptions in [[the Tomb]], which was the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] term for the primary Rakatan prison complex, it took the entire Infinite Empire to subdue the World Razer.<ref name="World Razer">{{TORcite|type=codex|The World Razer}}</ref>

Around [[27,700 BBY]], the Rakata discovered the planet [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] species. The Rakata showed the [[Sith King]] [[Adas]] the technology of [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]], but Adas soon realized the Empire's intentions of conquest and led his people in driving the Rakata off of Korriban.<ref name="Evil">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> The Rakata conquered a number of worlds in the region that was later known as the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], including the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], which was home to the [[Human/Legends|Human]] species. Despite their enslavement by the Rakata, however, the Humans experimented with [[Sleeper ship/Legends|sleeper ships]] around [[27,500 BBY]], seeding a number of planets in the Core Worlds and the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]&mdash;many of which were also conquered by the Rakata.<ref name="Atlas" />

During the Infinite Empire's reign, the [[Esh-kha]] species began to overrun a number of Rakatan slave worlds, leading the Empire to attack the Esh-kha. One Esh-kha named [[Hallow Voice]] appealed to the Rakata to spare his species, but the Rakata strung out negotiations until they had contained the Esh-kha and then captured Hallow Voice. The Esh-kha were all imprisoned on Belsavis, locked in stasis vaults.<ref name="Hallow Voice">{{TORcite|type=codex|Hallow Voice}}</ref> The Rakatan [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Soa]], also known as the Infernal One, was one of the rulers of the Infinite Empire, though he was ultimately imprisoned on Belsavis in what became known as the [[Eternity Vault]].<ref name="Eternity Vault">{{TORcite|type=operation|Eternity Vault}}</ref>

===Collapse===
{{Main|Rakatan Civil War}}
{{Quote|By definition, the Infinite Empire cannot "fall".|A [[Rakata monument]]|<ref name="TOR:C">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|Counterpoint|Hoth}}</ref>}}
The Force-based technology of the Rakata had profound consequences which led to the total collapse of the Infinite Empire. The Star Forge began feeding off its Rakatan masters' aggressive tendencies and created dark side energies that further corrupted its creators. After generations of galactic supremacy and control, the Infinite Empire began to fracture. Huge slave revolts erupted throughout the borders of the Empire along with various factions vying for control. This led to a [[Rakatan Civil War|civil war]] throughout Rakatan controlled space. Already weakened by warfare, the Rakata were suddenly struck by a deadly [[Rakatan plague|plague]] in [[25,200 BBY]] (possibly created by one of the slave species) that spread rapidly through their ranks due to their self-crafted genetic uniformity. The virulent disease nearly exterminated the Rakata and brought the Infinite Empire to its knees, but the worst was yet to come.

[[File:Infinite_Empire_JMGD.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Rakata of the Infinite Empire.]]
A mutation in the disease caused the Rakata to lose their connection and power in the Force. As the Force adepts were culled from the overall population, the Rakata lost their ability to manipulate their own advanced technology. The Rakatans were forced to adapt to using inferior technology. With their slave masters thus weakened, the populace of many enslaved worlds rebelled. The Infinite Empire began to collapse as member worlds such as Korriban began to expel their Rakatan masters. The all-but-destroyed Rakata could do nothing but abandon their conquests and retreat to the safety of their homeworld.

Various factions on the Rakatan homeworld vied for dominance over what was left of the Empire and so began a devastating civil war that destroyed all the cities and transformed the surface of the planet into chains of islands. The war almost led to the extinction of the Rakatan species and drove most of the surviving Rakata underground where they devolved into primitive tribal groups. Only a faction known as [[Elders (Rakatan)|The Elders]], who were descended from the priest caste of the Infinite Empire, recalled the true history and subsequent fall of their people. In the following centuries, the defunct Infinite Empire was erased from the records of its former labor forces. It was lost from the pages of galactic history until its rediscovery during the [[Jedi Civil War]], a few thousand years after the Rakatas' alleged extinction.

==Culture==
The Empire produced technological innovations such as [[Terraforming/Legends|terraforming]] machinery, semi-sentient [[Star Map]]s and computers, and the transmogrifying [[Star Forge]] (built in [[30,000 BBY]]). Among its many crimes were those of aggressive war, [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] on a massive scale, and the casual obliteration of member worlds such as [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

===Slavery===
[[File:TempleoftheAncientsconstruction.jpg|thumb|250px|Rakata supervising slaves building Temple of the Ancients]]
As they needed a large number of Force-sensitive beings for fueling their starships and pursue their conquest of the galaxy, the Rakata became well-known practitioners of slavery which was not only built on it but also dependent on it. They also used a lot of their slaves as a labor force to build their greatest achievements, as for the Star Forge, a massive shipyard that used the energy from stars to fuel itself. Some of the races they used included [[Nikto/Legends|Niktos]], [[Duros/Legends|Duros]], [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], [[Human/Legends|Humans]], [[Selkath/Legends|Selkath]], and many more. Eventually, slavery toppled their Empire when their subjects banded together in massive revolts.

The slaves were stripped of their identities and a letter of the [[Aurebesh/Legends|aurebesh]] alphabet was assigned to each of them, and then tattooed in various places of their bodies in case they were [[Dismemberment/Legends|dismembered]]. Slaves who displeased the Rakata were often eaten by their ruthless masters.

In addition, when a slave particularly strong in the Force was discovered by a Rakatan [[Predor]], the latter could train him as a [[Force Hound]]. They would become powerful Dark Side users, trained for the purpose of discovering planets highly attuned to the Force and their inhabitants for their masters.

==Astrography==
[[File:Rakatan_Empire_Atlas.jpg|thumb|Infinite Empire map]]
Due to the limitations of the [[Force-drive|Rakatan hyperdrive]] technology, the Infinite Empire consisted of over 500 worlds, despite its name.<ref name="History 5" /> However, they were scattered far and wide over the entire length of the Known Galaxy. All the below-mentioned planets have either a large and lush ecosystem, such as Kashyyyk or Honoghr, or a connection to the Force, like Korriban, Dantooine, or Dathomir, since the Rakatan hyperdrive was only able to home in on planets with these features.

==Behind the scenes==
In ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]],'' the [[Overseer (droid)|Overseer]] droid on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] makes explicit that the Rakata didn't speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]], the main language of humans, and that Humans weren't a slave species of the Rakata.<ref name="KOTOR" /> However, ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' and ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' mention humans being slaves of the Rakata<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="Atlas" /> and in ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi]]'', a Rakata named [[Tul'kar]] has a human slave named [[Tau (individual)|Xesh]].<ref name="DOTJ FS 1" />
